title: I Enforced the Professor's Laptop Ban on the Professor

parts.text: I put my notebook on the desk because Dr. Hale banned laptops, then watched him open his laptop. I am nineteen, freshman, broke, the job I wanted was this TA slot. The lecture hall smelled like dry-erase ghost and someone's tuna wrap. Hale had said screens destroy attention. He said it on a slide. Then he angled his lid and the projector accidentally mirrored his Amazon cart: Bluetooth soundbar, two-day shipping, coupon code HALE10. The class made that tiny sound. He slapped it shut. "Technical difficulties." He pointed at me because I was in the front, the desperate seat. "You. Collect phones." I said, "The syllabus says no devices for students." He smiled. "Don't be clever." I collected phones in a plastic bin that used to hold bulk pretzels, salt still in the corners. Mid-lecture his laptop chimed. An email from the department: TA applications due today, Hale to recommend. He glanced, then kept talking about Plato like Plato cared about soundbars. "I need someone who respects the room." I said, "The projector respected it for you." A girl named Noor snorted and then looked terrified. "If you want a recommendation, you'll sign the attendance sheet you missed while being cute." I had signed. Then he posted on the course page: any student who discusses class incidents online will be referred. I screenshotted the Amazon slide still in the lecture capture, because this school records everything and he had forgotten the capture light was red.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Lecture capture still has his Amazon cart, and he just threatened anyone who talks about it.

social.video_title: He banned laptops then mirrored Amazon — Part 1/2
social.description: A pretzel-salt phone bin, a HALE10 coupon, and a TA slot hanging on respect. The capture light was red. Would you have screenshot the lecture recording?

parts.text: I did not post the video. I emailed accessibility services and the department chair with a polite question: does the device ban apply to instructors when lecture capture is on? I attached the still, not the meme. Hale called me into the office that smells like orange peels in the trash. "You're making a career out of a joke," he said. I said, "I'm making a career out of a TA application due today." He typed, loudly. Then the chair, Dr. Okonkwo, appeared because she actually reads email. She asked Hale to follow his own syllabus in rooms that record. He agreed in the way of a man agreeing with weather. The referral threat came down. I got the TA slot for a different professor, which was better. Hale still bans laptops. He also puts a sticky note over the capture light, which is funny and sad. Noor brought me a tuna wrap as a joke and I ate it because I am broke. I wrote my first rec section on attention, and I did not mention soundbars. Students still tell the story. I tell them to read syllabi like contracts, because they are, even when the other party is shopping. My blue pen still blobs. I keep the still in a folder named Plato anyway. Not for revenge. For the day someone says it didn't happen. It happened. The coupon code probably still works, which is the most academic ending I can give you.

social.description: I asked a polite question with a still frame, not a meme. The TA slot moved to a better professor. Would you have eaten the tuna wrap?
